name: Vulnerable Java app
description: A Java class with hard-coded credentials, SQL built by concatenation, a shell command, MD5, unsafe deserialization and an unhardened XML parser. Intentionally insecure, for education.
expected: Findings from the Java token scanner. The path traversal and the secret returned from a method are not flagged (known misses).

fixes.title: Read credentials from the environment
fixes.explanation: The database password and API key come from environment variables (rotate the exposed values).
edits: private static final String DB_PASSWORD = System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD");
private static final String API_KEY = System.getenv("API_KEY");

fixes.title: Use a PreparedStatement
fixes.explanation: User input is bound as parameters instead of being concatenated into the SQL text.

fixes.title: Run a fixed program with an argument
fixes.explanation: ProcessBuilder runs one fixed program and passes the user value as a single argument; no shell parses it.
edits:
Runtime runtime = Runtime.getRuntime();
        Process process = runtime.exec(command);

fixes.title: Use SHA-256 instead of MD5
fixes.explanation: MD5 is broken for security use. (A real password store should use a slow password hash such as Argon2 or bcrypt.)

fixes.title: Do not deserialize untrusted bytes
fixes.explanation: The bytes are treated as text data instead of being turned back into Java objects.

fixes.title: Disable DOCTYPE processing in the XML parser
fixes.explanation: With DOCTYPE declarations disallowed, external entities cannot be defined.
